coded.vl: A labor statute applies with exclusions, or a sector-specific labor statute applies
coded.n: The Seafarers Act, a sector-specific labor statute, applies instead of the Labor Standards Act. It excludes fishing vessels under 20 tons that a Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries ordinance names.
coded.src: Seafarers Act Art. 3(1) proviso item 3
coded.g: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)

coded.vl: A separate floor applies that is lower than, or not linked to, the national minimum
coded.n: Wages for foreign crew are set by collective agreement between shipowners and the seafarers' union, below Korean crew; the Minister may set a seafarers' minimum wage (KRW 2,694,560 a month in 2026) and the Act draws no nationality line. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries notice setting the 2026 figure lets a collective agreement set the minimum for foreign crew, which is why the code is 1 (official guidance, not legislation).
coded.src: Seafarers Act Art. 59; Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Notice 2025-200 (official guidance); NHRCK recommendations to the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries; Korea Times, 12 Jul 2023
coded.g: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)

coded.vl: Excluded from working-time rules
coded.n: The Seafarers Act's working-time chapter (Chapter 6, including the Art. 60 hours and rest rules) does not apply to fishing vessels other than fish carriers. The Minister may set separate standards, but none were found in the Act or its Enforcement Rule. Recoded from 1 to 0 on 13 Nov 2026.
coded.src: Seafarers Act Arts 60, 68(1)(ii), 68(2); Enforcement Rule Art. 46
coded.g: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)

coded.vl: Cannot change without the employer's consent
coded.n: Placement runs through manning agencies; changing vessel needs the shipowner's release. Under review: the Immigration Act and the Ministry of Justice visa manual allow a change of vessel with the Ministry's prior permission on listed grounds, and no shipowner-consent rule was found in them, which would support a code of 1; the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries guideline requires repatriation when the contract ends. Editors to decide.
coded.src: NHRCK; EJF (2024); Immigration Act; Ministry of Justice visa manual and Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries guideline (official guidance)
coded.g: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)

coded.vl: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
coded.n: May join the Korean seafarers' union that negotiates their wages, but have little voice in it.
coded.src: Secondary sources
coded.g: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)

coded.vl: Fees charged to the worker are prohibited in the destination's law
coded.n: The Seafarers Act bars anyone who recruits, places or manages seafarers from taking money from them on any pretext, with no nationality limit, and penalizes breaches. Owners hiring through agencies in states outside the Maritime Labour Convention must check that the agency meets its standards. Fees charged by sending-country agencies remain an enforcement gap. Recoded from 1 to 2 on 13 Nov 2026.
coded.src: Seafarers Act Arts 111, 113(2); World Fishing / EJF, Mar 2024
coded.g: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)

coded.vl: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
coded.n: A statutory fishing-vessel crew accident insurance is compulsory for owners of covered vessels, replacing industrial accident insurance, with no nationality exclusion; registered foreign workers at covered workplaces are also enrolled in National Health Insurance. Distant-water and family-only vessels are excepted. Recoded from 1 to 2 on 13 Nov 2026 (coding judgment: the sector-specific statutory scheme is treated as the national scheme).
coded.src: Fishing Vessel Crew Insurance Act Arts 6, 16; National Health Insurance Act Art. 109(2)
coded.g: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)

coded.vl: Only general channels, or channels hard to reach from the workplace (for example at sea)
coded.n: General labor and maritime channels. In 2026 the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family issued indicators for identifying trafficking victims (often reported as forced-labor guidelines for migrant fishers).
coded.src: Ministry of Gender Equality and Family Notice 2026-32 (official guidance); Korea Times, 2 Sep 2026
coded.g: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)

coded.vl: May move to another status that can lead to permanent residence, on conditions
coded.n: E-10 holders may switch to the skilled-worker status (E-7-4) for long-term residence (confirmed by the Ministry of Justice, 22 Oct 2026). The Ministry's guidance sets the conditions: at least four years' stay, 200 points, annual income of KRW 25 million and Korean language level 2, with a quota of 33,000 for 2026.
coded.src: Ministry of Justice release, 22 Oct 2026; Ministry of Justice visa manual (official guidance)
coded.g: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)

coded.vl: Barred
coded.n: E-10 holders are not among the statuses whose spouses and children may receive the F-3 dependant visa.
coded.src: Immigration Act Enforcement Decree, Annex 1-2 item 25
coded.g: South Korea · crew of vessels of 20 tons and over (E-10)

changes.en: Employment Permit System starts under the Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers (2003); the industrial trainee system it replaced is abolished in 2007.
EU issues an IUU 'yellow card' to South Korea (lifted April 2015).
Supreme Court recognizes the Migrants' Trade Union.
Ratifies ILO C29, C87 and C98 (in force April 2022).
Government-to-government arrangement with Indonesia for fishers on coastal vessels.
Plan for distant-water crew: voyages capped at 12 months; companies to drop agencies that deduct wages.
Laos begins sending fishing crew on the E-10-2 visa.
Indicators for identifying trafficking victims issued by the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family (Notice 2026-32), applied to migrant fishers.
Ministry of Justice confirms a route for E-9 and E-10 workers to the skilled-worker status (E-7-4).

dec.n: Undocumented worker and industrial accident compensation
dec.pe: A foreign worker without the right papers was hurt at a factory in Korea and refused compensation. The Supreme Court said immigration status does not cancel his right to accident benefits.
dec.pi: Seorang pekerja asing tanpa dokumen yang sah terluka di sebuah pabrik di Korea dan ditolak kompensasinya. MA menyatakan status imigrasi tidak menghapus haknya atas tunjangan kecelakaan.

dec.n: Industrial trainees and the Labor Standards Act
dec.pe: Korea brought in foreign workers as “trainees” who worked like employees but without full labour rights. The Constitutional Court said this was unequal treatment.
dec.pi: Korea mendatangkan pekerja asing sebagai “peserta magang” yang bekerja seperti karyawan tetapi tanpa hak penuh. MK menyatakan ini perlakuan tidak setara.

dec.n: Limits on changing workplace under the Employment Permit System
dec.pe: Workers who come to Korea under the Employment Permit System can change employer only a few times. They asked the Constitutional Court to remove this limit. The Court kept it.
dec.pi: Pekerja yang datang ke Korea lewat Sistem Izin Kerja (EPS) hanya boleh beberapa kali pindah majikan. Mereka meminta MK menghapus batas itu. MK mempertahankannya.

dec.n: Seoul-Gyeonggi-Incheon Migrants’ Trade Union v. Minister of Labor
dec.pe: Migrant workers in Korea set up a union, but the government refused to register it because some members had no valid visa. After eight years in court, the Supreme Court said all people who work for wages are workers and may form unions.
dec.pi: Pekerja migran di Korea membentuk serikat, tetapi pemerintah menolak mendaftarkannya karena sebagian anggota tidak punya visa yang sah. Setelah delapan tahun di pengadilan, Mahkamah Agung menyatakan semua orang yang bekerja untuk upah adalah pekerja dan boleh membentuk serikat.

dec.n: Severance pay paid only after departure
dec.pe: Korea pays migrant workers’ severance only once they leave the country. Workers said this was unfair. The Constitutional Court kept the rule.
dec.pi: Korea membayar pesangon pekerja migran hanya setelah mereka meninggalkan negara itu. Pekerja menyebutnya tidak adil. MK mempertahankan aturan itu.

dec.n: Exclusion of farm workers from working-hours rules
dec.pe: A Cambodian farm worker in Korea challenged the rule that farm workers get no legal limits on hours or rest days. The Constitutional Court kept the rule.
dec.pi: Seorang pekerja pertanian asal Kamboja di Korea menggugat aturan bahwa pekerja pertanian tidak punya batas jam kerja atau hari libur. MK mempertahankan aturan itu.

dec.pe: Ten years after the first ruling, migrant workers again challenged the limits on changing employer. The Constitutional Court again kept them.
dec.pi: Sepuluh tahun setelah putusan pertama, pekerja migran kembali menggugat batas pindah majikan. MK kembali mempertahankannya.

dec.pe: Korea could keep foreigners in immigration detention with no time limit. The Constitutional Court said this was unconstitutional and told Parliament to fix the law.
dec.pi: Korea bisa menahan orang asing di detensi imigrasi tanpa batas waktu. MK menyatakan ini inkonstitusional dan meminta parlemen memperbaiki UU.
